docs.title: Code Generation
docs.summary: You get a working connector adapter in hours instead of weeks. Prism uses Grace, a code generation tool that reads payment provider API specs and produces Rust connector integration code with proper request/response transformations.

docs.title: Documentation Generation
docs.summary: You get API reference docs that stay current without anyone manually updating markdown files every time a field changes. Prism generates all /docs-generated content from the source proto definitions and a rules file that enforces consistency.

docs.title: SDK Generation
docs.summary: You get idiomatic SDKs in Node.js, Python, Java, Rust, and Go without maintaining five separate codebases. Prism generates language-specific bindings from the same protobuf definitions, ensuring every SDK stays synchronized with the core API.

docs.title: Test Generation
docs.summary: You get regression tests for every connector without writing them by hand. Prism generates test suites from the proto definitions and a declarative test spec, then runs them against live sandboxes to catch breaking changes before they hit production.

docs.title: ACH Direct Debit
docs.summary: Automated Clearing House direct debit. Debits funds from a US bank account using account and routing numbers. Used for USD payments in the United States.

docs.title: Apple Pay
docs.summary: Wallet payment using a tokenized card from the customer's Apple Wallet. The encrypted payment data is obtained from the Apple Pay JS API (or native SDK) on the client side — it is never constructed manually.

docs.title: Card
docs.summary: Raw card payment. The merchant collects card details directly and sends them to Prism. Requires PCI compliance — if you are not PCI compliant, use [Connector Token](./connector-token.md) instead.

docs.title: Connector Token
docs.summary: Used when card details are collected by the processor's JS SDK (e.g. Stripe.js, Adyen Drop-in). Raw card data never reaches your server — the processor returns an opaque token that Prism accepts directly.

docs.title: Google Pay
docs.summary: Wallet payment using a tokenized card stored in the customer's Google account. The encrypted payment token is obtained from the Google Pay JS API on the client side — it is never constructed manually.

docs.title: iDEAL
docs.summary: Dutch bank redirect payment method. The customer selects their bank and completes payment on the bank's page — no card details needed. Prism redirects to the bank via returnurl.

docs.title: Klarna
docs.summary: Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) payment method. The customer pays later or in instalments — Klarna handles the credit decision. Prism redirects to Klarna's hosted flow via returnurl.

docs.title: PayPal
docs.summary: Redirect-based wallet payment. The customer is redirected to PayPal to authenticate and approve the payment, then returned to your returnurl.

docs.title: Payment Methods
docs.summary: Prism's authorize call accepts a paymentmethod that describes how the payer's instrument is represented. Set exactly one variant inside that object — Prism handles the connector-specific transformation.

docs.title: SEPA Direct Debit
docs.summary: Single Euro Payments Area direct debit. Debits funds directly from the customer's EU bank account using their IBAN. Used for EUR payments across eurozone countries.
